messages:
SLO Alert Bot: [ALERT] p99 latency spike on route /v1/generate in us-west1. p99 > 1.0s (SLO 250ms). p95 creeping up ~450ms. Streaming stalls: increased client disconnects and stalled event streams. Dashboard: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/latency/realtime?orgId=1&panelId=7

PagerDuty: Incident RD-20260315-1725607890 created and notified: dev-oncall rotation.

Devon R (oncall): on it. quick checklist:
  1) confirm traffic spike or error rate.
  2) check recent deploys in last 30m.
  3) verify KV cache hitrate and batching metrics.

Devon R (oncall): running quick queries:
```shell
# grafana link with query presets (p95/p99)
curl -s 'https://metrics.internal/api/v1/query?query=histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket{route="/v1/generate"}[5m])) by (le))'
```

Devon R (oncall): raw check shows p99 ~1.25s, p95 ~480ms. error-rate low but streaming stalls rising (~0.8% of streams).

Alex K: I noticed runtime-1.4.2 rolled into us-west1 ~12m ago. there were batching microchanges in that build. could be regression in continuous batching or kv eviction behavior.

Maria L: customer impact: Support reported 3 enterprise customers with timeouts and partial streams. opened TKT-1149 and started incident emails. tagging CSMs.

SRE Bot: auto-note: New host scale=+0 triggered 11m ago in us-west1; no autoscaler errors.

Devon R (oncall): quick mitigation suggestions:
  - route a small % (10-20%) to fallback model variant (lower memory, no aggressive batching).
  - temporarily increase backend pool by 1 node to absorb tail.
  - bump streaming keepalive to avoid premature stalls.

Alex K: I can flip fallback route. running CLI:
```bash
redwood route update --name generate --fallback-model rwd-small-v1 --weight 0.15 --region us-west1 --reason 'live mitigation: p99 spike'
```

Alex K: fallback routing applied. monitoring...

Devon R (oncall): also starting a controlled rollback of runtime-1.4.2 in us-west1 to runtime-1.4.1. rolling back canary first.
```bash
deploy rollback --cluster us-west1 --service runtime --to-tag runtime-1.4.1 --strategy canary --percent 20
```

Ops:Oncall: FYI we've notified legal for potential SLA impact if >30 min.

~6 minutes later~

Devon R (oncall): observed metrics after routing + partial rollback: p95 -> 190ms (was 480ms), p99 -> 230ms (was 1.25s). streaming stall rate down to 0.12%. looks like mitigation is effective.

Maria L: confirming customer tickets updated: TKT-1149 notes temporary mitigation; customers advised to retry. CSMs notified.

Alex K: continuing rollback to 100% in us-west1 to fully remove runtime-1.4.2.
```bash
deploy rollback --cluster us-west1 --service runtime --to-tag runtime-1.4.1 --strategy immediate
```

SRE Bot: rollback completed. health checks green.

Devon R (oncall): p99 stable under SLO for last 3m. marking initial incident mitigation successful. started post-incident ticket: RINC-20260315-1725607890 for deep dive (suspect batching scheduler regression + cache evictions).

Maria L: action items for postmortem:
  - production trace of batching scheduler behavior across runtime-1.4.2 changes. owner: Alex K
  - reproduce streaming stall locally with high-concurrency harness. owner: Devon R
  - add automated alerting for streaming stall % (threshold 0.5%) and tie to runbook. owner: SRE team

Devon R (oncall): handoff: I'm wrapping up initial triage. leaving incident open for postmortem owners. passing to Alex K for follow-up analysis and timeline reconstruction.

Alex K: acknowledged. will own the RCA and follow-up commit/PR to revert batching heuristics. ETA for summary draft: EOD.

Devon R (oncall): final note: no widespread data loss reported. customer impact limited to elevated tail latency and transient stream stalls for a small subset. will update incident channel when postmortem is filed. :white_check_mark:

Ops:Oncall: Incident RD-20260315-1725607890 set to monitored -> resolved when RCA posted.
